full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Quddus, J: This is an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for anticipatory bail of the petitioner in Halisohor Police Station Case No. 25 dated 26.12.2016 corresponding to GR No. 282 of 2016 under sections 409, 420 and 109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. 

 3. Mr. Md. Anowarul Islam, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the allegation made in the FIR is absolutely false and has been made for collateral purpose out of political grudge against the petitioner's husband and one of the co-accused in the present case Md. Aslam Chowdhury, a detained leader of Bangladesh Nationalist Party having cut-throat rivalry with the party in power. It has been lodged only for harassment and humiliation to them, not for securing the ends of justice. With reference to the annexure A series to the supplementary affidavit, Mr. Islam submits that prior to lodging the FIR the time-frame for repayment of the loan has been rescheduled by the bank concerned converting it into four years term loan. The petitioner or her company is, therefore, not a defaulter. So, the question of misappropriation of loan money does not arise. 

 5. Mr. Islam lastly submits that since no charge sheet has yet been submitted and no cognizance is taken by the Special Judge, the petitioner has no forum to surrender. There is no practice of granting bail by the Metropolitan Magistrates in such type of cases. On that count Mr. Islam makes a prayer for granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner till submission of police report. 

 6. Mr. Nazibur Rahman, learned Deputy Attorney General and Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate for the ACC oppose the prayer for bail in one voice and submit that there is allegation of misappropriation of crores of public money against the petitioner and her company. It is not a fit case for anticipatory bail. 

 7. In addition to that Mr. Khan while referring to the case of Durnity Daman Commission and another Vs. Dr. Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain and another, 66 DLR (AD) 92 submits that the High Court Division cannot grant anticipatory bail to an accused for a period more than four weeks. 

 8. In reply thereto Mr. Islam submits that the South East Bank Ltd. is a pure and simple private bank and as such the capital/money invested/deposited in it cannot be termed as public money. He also points out the factual position of the said case that differs from the present one. 

 10. The petitioner being implicated in another criminal case of the same nature, earlier moved in this Court with Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 23559 of 2016, wherein we granted her anticipatory bail till submission of investigation report by order dated 31.07.2016. Challenging the said order, the ACC moved in the Appellate Division with Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 757 of 2016. After hearing, the Appellate Division summarily rejected the leave petition by order dated 22.10.2016 and thereby affirmed the order of the High Court Division (vide annexure B and B-1 to the supplementary affidavit). 

 11. The creditor South East Bank Ltd. is a private bank, not a public or nationalized one. Even the State/Government has no share in it. The capital invested and money deposited in the bank and the profit generated therefrom belong to its individual shareholders and depositors, not to the treasury department or any Governmental body or any statutory Public authority. We, therefore, do not accept the contention of Mr. Khan that the money allegedly misappropriated is public money to import more gravity in the alleged offence. It is a common perception that corruption is alarmingly growing in all Public offices and the People are not getting any service without meeting the naked demand of bribe from a section of Government servants. We expect ACC to be more active in right direction to prosecute the cases, where 'public money' is misappropriated, and the offences of criminal misconduct are committed by the Government officials irrespective of their position, power and inclination. 

 12. The facts and circumstances of the present case clinched with the socio-political culture prevailing in our country thus give an indication that this case has been initiated with an ulterior motive and collateral purpose, not for securing the ends of justice. 

 13. Let us examine the point raised by Mr. Khan that the High Court Division cannot grant anticipatory bail for more than four weeks in any case. His submission is point-blank with no explanation to judicial reasons. On this point our Appellate Division in the landmark case of State Vs. Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 242 has observed: 

 "Anticipatory bail should be granted by the High Court Division for a limited period or till filing of the charge-sheet whichever is appropriate in the circumstances of the case. After expiry of the period or filing of the charge-sheet, as the case may be, the accused must appear before the Court concerned and obtain fresh bail from the Court on the merit of the case." 

 14. The above quoted view has also been reflected in the case of Salauddin Abdul Samad Shaikh Vs. State of Maharashtra, CDJ 1995 SC 1284, wherein the Supreme Court of India observed: 

 "Anticipatory bail is granted in anticipation of arrest in non-bailable cases, but that does not mean that the regular Court, which is to try the offender, is sought to be bypassed and that is the reason why the High Court very rightly fixed the outer date for the continuance of the bail and on the date of its expiry directed the petitioner to move the regular Court for bail. That is the correct procedure to follow because it must be realized that when the Court of Session or the High Court is granting anticipatory bail, it is granted at a stage when the investigation is incomplete and, therefore, it is not it about the nature of evidence against the alleged offender. It is, therefore, necessary that such anticipatory bail orders should be of a limited duration only and ordinarily on the expiry of that duration or extended duration of the Court granting anticipatory bail should leave it to the regular Court to deal with the matter on an appreciation of evidence placed before it after the investigation has made progress or the charge-sheet is submitted." 

 15. We have also gone through the case of Durnity Daman Commission and another Vs. Dr. Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain and another, 66 DLR (AD) 92 as cited by the learned Advocate for the ACC. In the said case, the case of Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury has been referred to, but the proposition regarding the period of anticipatory bail as quoted above has not been overruled. However, in the latter the period of anticipatory bail has been dealt with in the following manner: 

 16. The above quoted view taken in the case of Dr. Khandaker Mosharraf Hussain does not restrain the High Court Division from exercising judicial discretion of granting anticipatory bail for a period more than four weeks, if the circumstance demands. It rather gives a clear indication that anticipatory bail can be granted up to submission of charge sheet. 

 17. It is a well settled and all-accepted proposition of law that anticipatory bail can be granted in a case initiated with an ulterior motive only to harass and humiliate the accused, not to secure the ends of justice. If the High Court Division by a proper and intelligent scrutiny' thinks a case to be of such type and grant anticipatory bail to a prima-facie innocent accused, why it should push her/him toward harassment and humiliation after expiry of four weeks. The sense of justice says that in such a case an accused should be protected from unnecessary harassment until the Court, which is to take cognizance of offence, is equipped with all prosecution materials gathered by way of an exhaustive investigation. The Court cannot mechanically ignore the agony of a justice seeker. 

 18. Under the above premise we find it difficult to accept the submission of the learned Advocate for the ACC that the High Court Division cannot grant anticipatory bail for a period more than four weeks even in an appropriate and fit case. This is a matter of judicial discretion, which should not be restricted. 

 19. We are, therefore, inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner till submission of investigation report in the instant case. 

 20. The purpose of issuing a Rule is to hear the other side. In the case in hand, since advance copies of the application have been served upon the opposite parties, and the learned Deputy Attorney General as well as the learned Advocate for the ACC have appeared and made their submissions, we think this application can fairly be disposed of without issuing any Rule. 

 21. Accordingly, the accused-petitioner Jamila Najnil Mawla is enlarged on anticipatory bail in Halisohor Police Station Case No.25 dated 26.12.2016 corresponding to.GR No. 282 of 2016 under sections 409, 420 and 109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 till submission of the investigation report on furnishing bail bond to the satisfaction of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong.
